stem: A call center application displays customer information to support agents. To protect customer privacy, the application replaces the first five digits of the customer's Social Security Number with asterisks on the screen. Which data protection method is this?

A company is rolling out new laptops that require full-disk encryption. The security policy mandates that the encryption keys must be bound to the specific hardware of the laptop and protected against offline dictionary attacks. Which component is BEST suited to fulfill this requirement?

A corporate IT department manages multiple subdomains, including mail.company.com, portal.company.com, and vpn.company.com. They want to secure all of these with a single digital certificate to simplify administration. Which type of certificate BEST meets this requirement?

A cryptanalyst is evaluating two different implementations of the RSA algorithm, one using a 1024-bit key and the other using a 4096-bit key. What is the MOST significant operational tradeoff when selecting the longer key?

options.text: Increased administrative overhead for certificate authorities
Decreased availability of symmetric key exchange mechanisms
Increased processing time for encryption and decryption operations
Decreased compatibility with modern web browsers

stem: A government agency dictates that it must be able to decrypt communications of certain entities if a lawful order is issued. To facilitate this without possessing the entities' daily operating keys, a trusted third party holds a copy of the keys. What is this arrangement called?

A healthcare organization manages a massive patient registry. Instead of encrypting the entire server drive, the security team decides to encrypt the underlying SQL data structures to protect the data at rest while allowing the OS to run normally. Which encryption level is being applied?

A high-traffic web server requires real-time validation of client certificates without having to download and parse large, static lists of revoked serial numbers. Which protocol should the organization implement to achieve this?

A large enterprise is migrating from a decentralized authentication model to a framework that heavily relies on digital certificates for user login, device authentication, and secure email. What framework is the organization expanding?

A major financial institution needs to generate and manage high-value root certificates for its enterprise PKI. The keys must be stored in a dedicated, tamper-resistant network appliance with strong physical security controls. Which of the following should be deployed?

A manager places a sensitive document into a shared departmental folder. The manager wants to ensure that even if other employees have network access to the folder, only authorized individuals can open and read this specific document. Which encryption strategy is BEST?

A retail merchant wants to store customer credit card data for recurring billing but wishes to reduce the scope of PCI DSS compliance. Instead of storing the actual PAN (Primary Account Number), the merchant's system stores a randomly generated string of characters provided by the payment gateway. What technique is being utilized?

A security analyst is selecting an encryption algorithm to protect archives of video surveillance footage. The primary constraints are high speed and low processing overhead. Which cryptographic approach should be selected?

A smartphone application processes highly sensitive biometric data for user authentication. To protect this data from being accessed by the main operating system or other malicious apps, where should the cryptographic operations and biometric data be isolated?

A software development team writes a proprietary algorithm in JavaScript that runs in the client's browser. To make it difficult for competitors to reverse-engineer the logic, they intentionally scramble the variable names and code structure. Which technique is this an example of?
A storage administrator creates a unified logical storage area spanning multiple physical disks and applies encryption to the entire logical area. What type of encryption is this?

A supply chain organization wants to track the provenance of goods. They implement a decentralized, distributed system where every transaction is cryptographically linked to the previous one in a continuously growing list of records. Which technology is MOST likely being deployed?

A system administrator mounts a virtual encrypted disk file that acts as a logical drive within the operating system. All files written into this logical drive are automatically encrypted. This is an implementation of which encryption level?

A system needs to encrypt large volumes of backup data quickly before transmitting it to offsite storage. Why would the organization choose a symmetric algorithm over an asymmetric one for this specific task?

options.text: Symmetric algorithms provide inherent non-repudiation for the backup files
Symmetric algorithms do not require key management or secure key storage
Symmetric algorithms are less computationally intensive and much faster for bulk data
Symmetric algorithms use two separate keys, making them natively more secure

stem: A systems administrator is configuring a small internal test server and does not want to pay for or deploy an enterprise PKI. The administrator generates a digital certificate directly on the server for HTTPS access. What type of certificate has been created?

A user needs to securely store a specific tax document on a shared network drive where other users have read access to the directory. Which encryption level is MOST appropriate for this single document?

A user's laptop was stolen, and the client certificate installed on it could be compromised. The PKI administrator revokes the certificate. How do other systems typically learn that this certificate is no longer valid?

options.text: By forcing a key exchange protocol
By examining the Root of trust
By checking a Certificate Revocation List (CRL)
By querying the hardware security module

stem: A web administrator needs to renew an expiring digital certificate for a company web server. What MUST the administrator generate on the web server and send to the Certificate Authority to obtain the new certificate?
A web application backend utilizes Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) to protect the entire SQL instance. Which level of encryption does TDE operate at?

A website administrator wants to ensure that a downloadable software patch has not been modified by an attacker in transit. The administrator posts a string of characters next to the download link. Users are instructed to run a specific algorithm against the downloaded file and compare the resulting string. What cryptographic mechanism is being used?

An administrator configures a server with one hard drive split into two distinct logical sections: one for the OS and one for storing sensitive log files. If the administrator only encrypts the section containing the log files, which level of encryption is being utilized?

An application requires that only the Social Security Number fields within a customer table be encrypted, while the rest of the customer table remains plaintext for rapid searching. Which level of encryption MUST be implemented to achieve this?

An attacker has stolen a database containing user password hashes. To mitigate the threat of offline brute-force and rainbow table attacks, the application's developers previously configured the hashing algorithm to iterate thousands of times before outputting the final hash. What defense mechanism is this?
An auditor mandates that all administrative traffic between an administrator's workstation and a core switch must be encrypted. Implementing SSH to replace Telnet addresses security at which level?

An e-commerce company is launching a public-facing website. To ensure that visitors' web browsers implicitly trust the site without security warnings, from where should the company obtain their digital certificate?
An employee wants to receive an encrypted email from a vendor. Which cryptographic component MUST the employee share with the vendor to facilitate this secure communication?

An enterprise utilizes various cloud providers, internal servers, and containerized applications. They need a centralized service to create, rotate, disable, and define access controls for all cryptographic keys across these environments. What is the MOST appropriate solution to implement?

An operating system is installed on the primary drive, while all proprietary company data is stored on a secondary drive. To optimize boot performance while securing the data at rest, only the secondary drive is encrypted. What type of encryption is this?

An organization wants to ensure that encrypted company data can still be recovered if an employee unexpectedly leaves the company and their encryption keys are lost. Which of the following BEST describes the solution to this problem?

During a forensic investigation, an analyst discovers that a malicious insider has been exfiltrating corporate secrets by hiding text data within the pixels of marketing images posted to a public website. What concept does this activity illustrate?
During a security review, a consultant recommends replacing DES with AES-256 for all internal database encryption. What is the PRIMARY reason for upgrading the cryptographic algorithm?

options.text: To enable digital signatures on the database tables
To utilize an algorithm that is computationally resistant to modern brute-force attacks
To transition from a symmetric to an asymmetric methodology
To comply with requirements for utilizing hardware security modules

stem: If a corporate laptop is stolen from a coffee shop, which cryptographic solution provides the BEST protection against an attacker removing the hard drive to read the operating system and user files?

In a multi-tenant cloud environment, a database administrator ensures that each tenant's specific data rows are encrypted with a unique key, preventing one tenant from accessing another's data even within the same table. Which encryption strategy provides this granularity?
In a PKI, what is the PRIMARY role of a Certificate Authority (CA)?

options.text: To issue, manage, and validate digital certificates
To continuously monitor network traffic for malicious activity
To symmetrically encrypt the data payload of network packets
To provide a secure physical vault for key escrow

stem: In an asymmetric encryption scenario, if Alice wants to send a confidential message to Bob, which key does Alice use to encrypt the message so that only Bob can read it?

In hardware-backed security, which component provides the foundational security layer from which all other secure operations, such as secure boot and cryptographic key generation, derive their assurance?

Two remote servers must establish a secure session over an untrusted network without transmitting the actual session key across the link. Which cryptographic mechanism BEST facilitates this requirement?
What distinguishes asymmetric encryption from symmetric encryption regarding key management?

options.text: Asymmetric encryption uses the same key for both encryption and decryption
Asymmetric encryption requires hardware security modules for all key generation
Asymmetric encryption completely eliminates the need to manage any keys
Asymmetric encryption uses a mathematically related key pair, eliminating the need to securely distribute a shared secret

stem: What is the PRIMARY disadvantage of relying solely on full-disk encryption to protect data on a running, unlocked workstation?

options.text: It does not protect data from unauthorized users who access the active session
It requires the use of self-signed certificates
It cannot be managed by an enterprise key management system

stem: What is the PRIMARY purpose of establishing a PKI within an enterprise network?

options.text: To manage the creation, storage, and distribution of digital certificates
To ensure that all network traffic is encrypted using IPsec
To centralize the authentication of users via LDAP
To provide a symmetric key distribution system for legacy applications

stem: When a software developer digitally signs an executable file to prove it has not been tampered with, which cryptographic element is used to create the mathematical signature?
When a web browser connects to a secure website, what does the server present to the client to prove its identity and provide its public key?

When designing a database architecture, the security team must decide whether to encrypt the entire storage array or just the specific columns containing credit card numbers. This decision represents a choice regarding which cryptographic concept?

When implementing a robust cryptographic strategy, an organization decides to deploy a combination of software-based utilities and hardware appliances. What is the MOST important consideration when selecting these cryptographic tools?

options.text: Ensuring they only support self-signed certificates
Ensuring they rely entirely on proprietary, closed-source algorithms
Ensuring they bypass the operating system's native entropy sources
Ensuring they securely generate, store, and manage cryptographic keys

stem: When performing an audit of user credentials, a security engineer notices that two users have the exact same plaintext password, but their password hashes stored in the database are completely different. What technique was applied to the passwords prior to hashing to cause this?
Which BEST describes the fundamental difference between encryption and hashing?

options.text: Encryption provides integrity, while hashing provides confidentiality
Encryption is a two-way reversible process, while hashing is a one-way mathematical function
Encryption is used exclusively for data at rest, while hashing is used for data in transit
Encryption always relies on symmetric algorithms, while hashing uses asymmetric algorithms

stem: Which characteristic distinguishes an open public ledger from a traditional centralized database in the context of cryptographic transaction records?

options.text: Transactions in an open public ledger are entirely encrypted and hidden from all participants
The ledger allows anyone to view the transaction history and participate in the consensus mechanism
The ledger relies on a single trusted third party to validate and record all transactions
Transactions can be easily modified or deleted by network administrators after being recorded

stem: Which of the following cryptographic concepts provides authentication, integrity, and non-repudiation for an electronic document?
Which of the following mechanisms is BEST suited for authenticating people rather than systems?
Which of the following MUST be kept absolutely secret and heavily protected to maintain the integrity of a digital signature system?

options.text: The hash of the signed document

stem: Which of the following processes translates plaintext into ciphertext using a mathematical algorithm and a cryptographic key, primarily to ensure data confidentiality?
